resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rowlett dates the Rubicon Point light to 1916. The Lighthouse Service Bulletin of 1 October 1919 (PDF p. 39, printed p. 95) lists 'Rubicon Point, Lake Tahoe, Calif., flashing white' among the lights established, and the Commissioner's reports for fiscal 1917 and 1919 say no appropriation had been made for the lake's aids. The sources read do not settle when the Rubicon Point light was first lit, and the story says so. Rubicon Point is a separate station from this one.

notes_for_editor: No keeper is named for this light in any source read, and the USLHS roster has no place match (the nearest, Pigeon Point, is a different station); keepers and wrecks are left empty. Conflicts: (1) The station record says status inactive and the tower standing; the park information sheet calls the light operating, and Rowlett says the original tower was reportedly removed in 1985. (2) A Wikipedia article (a lead only, not cited) says the light was discontinued in 1935 and relit in 1936 at a cost of $590.52; no source read confirms this, the Lighthouse Service Bulletins 1922-1939 searched through the corpus have no Sugar Pine entry, and a newspaper search of 1922-1963 found nothing; check the 1930s Bulletins and Commissioner reports by page image before using any 1935 or 1936 date. (3) The county is unresolved: the record has none, the Wikipedia lead says El Dorado County, and California State Parks lists the park in El Dorado and Placer counties; left out of the story. (4) Rowlett's directory gives the Rubicon Point light a 1916 date. The bulletin of 1 October 1919 (PDF p. 39, printed p. 95) lists 'Rubicon Point, Lake Tahoe, Calif., flashing white' under Lights established; the OCR interleaves the name with a rescue narrative, so the name was read from the page image on 2026-10-28. The phrase 'Lake Tahoe, Calif., flashing white' is clean OCR. The story calls the bulletin issue by its date (1 October 1919) and does not say the entry falls in October. (5) The 1920 construction table (printed p. 100) is OCR'd in separate column blocks; the station name is matched by its line in the table, and no cost is used. (6) The AP dispatch's superintendent is printed as 'II. V. Rhodes' in OCR; the name is left out of the story. (7) The Lighthouse Circuit page claims a Corps of Engineers series and an automated acetylene beacon; neither is sourced, so neither is used. (8) The station's record range of 8 nm and the 'Fl W 4s' characteristic are not confirmed by a read source; Rowlett gives 'white flash every 4 s'. (9) The station photo on the record is 'Golden Hour at Emerald Bay' and does not show this light. (10) Rowlett's Rubicon Point entry (ARLHS USA-917; a 12 ft wood tower, inactive since 1921) describes a separate structure that needs its own record if it is queued.
